# **I. Project Overview** {#i.-project-overview}

## **1\. Scope and Purpose** {#1.-scope-and-purpose}

The primary objective of the EcoLink project is to build an Intelligent Recyclable Waste Classification and Trade Matching System. The project addresses two core environmental challenges in Vietnam: a widespread lack of household waste-sorting knowledge and the absence of an efficient, economically viable channel connecting households with local scrap collectors and recycling facilities. By combining Computer Vision (AI) image recognition, localized sorting instructions, GPS-based location matching, and gamification incentives, EcoLink transforms routine waste disposal into an engaging, eco-friendly, and financially rewarding habit. 

Architected as a responsive web application, EcoLink incorporates several key functional modules within its core scope. The system features AI-driven waste classification capable of identifying 8 to 12 common categories of recyclable waste using trained YOLOv8 or CNN models. This classification triggers a localized sorting rule engine that delivers dynamic, step-by-step cleaning and disposal instructions. Furthermore, households can list recyclable waste while discovering nearby verified recyclers through spatial querying using PostgreSQL/PostGIS. Trade coordination is managed end-to-end through a structured workflow—from initial request to acceptance, receipt confirmation, and completion or cancellation.

## **6\. Risks and Mitigations**  {#6.-risks-and-mitigations}

| \# | Risk | Prob | Impact | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **R01** | **Low AI Accuracy for Ambiguous / Damaged Waste**  *AI fails to correctly distinguish crumpled paper, dirty plastic, or complex items.* | Medium | High | **1\.** Restrict initial model scope to 8–12 well-defined recyclable classes. **2\.** Enforce a 60% confidence threshold to prompt user confirmation if uncertain. **3\.** Supplement public datasets with 40% self-collected real-world local photos. |
| **R02** | **Network Latency / Service Outage during Live Demo**  *Cloud AI API endpoint fails or lags during supervisor or board defense.* | Medium | High | **Convert trained model (TensorFlow.js / TFLite)** to run locally as an offline backup inside the client browser, ensuring the  core recognition feature works without the internet. |
| **R03** | **Scope Creep & Late Requirement Changes**  *Uncontrolled additions of complex features (e.g., online payments, native apps).* | Medium | High | **1\.** Formally freeze SRS after Week 5 review. **2\.** Explicitly list Exclusions (LI-01 to LI-10) in Report 1 & 3\. **3\.** Require impact analysis and supervisor approval for any Change Request. |
| **R04** | **PostGIS Spatial Matching Performance Bottleneck**  *Slow response when searching for recyclers by GPS coordinates under heavy load.* | Low | Medium | **1\.** Apply GiST spatial indexing on PostGIS location columns. **2\.** Cache active recycler profiles and geographic coordinates in Redis In-Memory cache. |
| **R05** | **Insufficient Real-World User & Recycler Survey Data**  *Difficulty reaching enough local scrap collectors (vựa ve chai) for survey data.* | Medium | Medium | **1\.** Assign a dedicated 3-member sub-team (Luan, Duong, Hoang). **2\.** Conduct direct field interviews at local scrap yards in Hanoi. **3\.** Utilize online Google Forms targeting eco-conscious communities. |

# **II. Management Approach** {#ii.-management-approach}

## **1\. Project Process/Methodology** {#1.-project-process/methodology}

The EcoLink project applies a **Hybrid Software Development Methodology**, combining **Waterfall** for project initiation, requirement freezing, and design phases with **Agile/Scrum Iterative Development** for software implementation. This approach ensures structured compliance with academic milestones while maintaining flexibility during feature implementation.  
**Initiation & Requirement Planning Phase (Weeks 1–3):**

* Establish core team roles, set up Git repositories, and align with Supervisor (Mr. Ta Dinh Tien).  
* Conduct real-world user surveys, perform gap analysis against existing market solutions, and formalize the Software Requirement Specification (SRS v0.9/v1.0) and Project Management Plan (PMP).

**Architecture & Detailed Design Phase (Weeks 4–5):**

* Build a Vertical Prototype / Proof of Concept (POC) for the Python FastAPI YOLOv8 AI Vision Service.  
* Construct System Design Specifications (SDS v1.0), ERD schemas, API inventories, and Test Plans.

**Iterative Implementation Phase (Weeks 6–11):**

* **Iteration 1 (Weeks 6–7):** Core Backend setup (.NET Clean Architecture), JWT Authentication, AI Image Classification API, and Rule Engine mapping.  
* **Iteration 2 (Weeks 8–9):** PostGIS Geolocation matching, Recycler discovery, Waste listing management, and Trade request workflows.  
* **Iteration 3 (Weeks 10–11):** Virtual tree gamification ("Green Points"), Eco Facts, Leaderboards, Admin Dashboard, and AI Misclassification feedback loop.

**Verification, Validation & Freeze Phase (Weeks 12–13):**

* Execute System Testing, Integration Testing, Performance/Latency verification, and User Manual writing.  
* Final freeze of source code and deployment artifacts.

**Project Closing Phase (Week 14):**

* Finalize Capstone Project Report (Report 7\) and conduct final presentation defense.

## **2\. Quality Management** {#2.-quality-management}

To achieve the project metrics defined in Section I (such as ≥ 85% AI top-1 classification accuracy, web page load time ≤ 2.0 s, and zero high-severity defects), the team enforces quality controls across four core dimensions:

### **2.1 Defect Prevention & Code Standards** {#2.1-defect-prevention-&-code-standards}

* **Clean Architecture Compliance:** Enforce strict separation of layers in the .NET solution (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, WebApi) so that domain logic remains independent of external frameworks.  
* **Code Reviews:** Every Pull Request (PR) merged into the main branch requires at least one code review and approval by the Tech Lead (Thang) or Sub-leader (Giang).  
* **Static Analysis:** Apply standard linter tools (Roslyn analyzers for C\# .NET and PEP8 / Flake8 for Python FastAPI).

### **2.2 Testing Levels & Validation** {#2.2-testing-levels-&-validation}

* **Unit Testing:** Write unit tests for business handlers, CQRS services, and rule mapping calculations using xUnit (.NET).  
* **Integration Testing:** Test API endpoints, EF Core database mappings, PostGIS spatial queries, and inter-service communication between .NET Web API and Python FastAPI.  
* **AI Model Validation:** Evaluate model accuracy on a dedicated test dataset using Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and Confusion Matrix analysis. Enforce an Out-of-Distribution threshold (\$\< 60\\%\$ confidence) to trigger re-capture prompts for invalid images.  
* **Offline Backup Validation:** Maintain a converted lightweight model (TensorFlow.js / TFLite) as a client-side fallback during live demonstrations to mitigate network outage risks.

## **6\. Configuration Management** {#6.-configuration-management}

### **6.1 Document Management** {#6.1-document-management}

**Centralized Storage:** All project documents (proposal, SRS, SDS, weekly reports, user guides) are stored and collaborated on via Google Drive (SEP490\_G141\_FA26).  
**File Naming Convention:** Documents follow the strict naming structure:  
\[Document\_Name\]\_\[Group\_ID\]\_\[Version\]\_\[Date\]  
*Example:* Report1\_SEP490\_G141\_v1.0.docx, Report2\_Project\_Tracking\_SEP490\_G141.xlsx.  
**Version Control Rules:**

* v0.x: Draft versions created during team working sessions.  
* v1.0, v2.0: Finalized versions approved by the Leader (Thang) and submitted to the Lecturer.

**Audit Trail:** Any modification to milestone documents must be recorded in the **Record of Changes / Change Log** table at the beginning of each report.

### **6.2 Source Code Management** {#6.2-source-code-management}

**Version Control System:** Source code is hosted on GitHub across two dedicated repositories:

* Backend & AI Service: VPGreenLight/intelligent-waste-sorting-trading  
* Frontend Web: VP GreenLight/ecolink-web

**Branching Strategy (Git Flow):**

* main: Production-ready code; protected branch requiring approval from Tech Lead (Thang) or Sub-leader (Giang).  
* develop: Integration branch where features are combined and tested.  
* feature/\[feature-id\]: Working branch for specific use cases (e.g., feature/FE-01-ai-scan, feature/FE-06-postgis-matching).  
* bugfix/\[bug-id\]: Branch for resolving issues identified during testing.

**Pull Request (PR) & Commit Rules:**

* Commit messages must follow the format: \[FE-xx/UC-xx\] \<type\>: \<description\> (e.g., \[FE-01\] feat: integrate YOLOv8 classification endpoint).  
* Every Pull Request requires at least one code review and approval from Leader/Sub-leader before merging into develop or main.
